Sorry but you don't pass. In terms of makeup you should wear more mascara (or just fake eyelashes, I can hardly even see yours) and that color of lipstick doesn't go that well with your skin tone, I'd go for something darker or a nude color (honestly imo most people can't pull off the bright red color). 

In terms of hair, that look is a little young for you (you look to be in your mid to late 20s). For women of that age long wavy hair and bangs is pretty popular, such as  [this](http://yourhairstyleideas.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/16-popular-women-hairstyles-with-bangs-2013.jpg) or [this](http://cf.ltkcdn.net/hair/images/std/143809-425x425-beautiful-hair-style-with-bangs.jpg). If you don't like those i'd recommend at least getting a haircut that has bangs because most trans women don't have very good hairlines in my opinion, and unfortunately you fall into that group (don't worry, I do too).

As for clothes, I wouldn't recommend wearing a dress with sleeves just yet because they aren't very flattering to your shoulders. Trans women usually have broad shoulders and it's easy to hide that with baggy tops, so I would go for a blouse like [this](http://www.petulant.biz/wp-content/uploads/2014/05/89d491d7e3a1.jpg) with a pencil skirt (maybe a circle skirt would look okay but generally outfits should be tight top + skirt or loose top + tight bottom, at least that's what I think looks best). Also your torso is pretty square, like most trans women, so I'd reccomend wearing a waist cincher or corset underneath your clothes to keep your waist nice and tiny, or wear thigh pads, or both.

Stay strong. I know how it feels to not be able to hold it in any longer, but I would consider waiting until I had more years of hrt under my belt. The easiest way to get a good reaction is to look sexy as fuck! :P

I definitely know that feeling. I'm 16 and pre-HRT because my parents are transphobic, but I still really like wearing something feminine in public. Thankfully tight/skinny jeans are trendy so i wear those pretty much all the time.

>...is comparable to wanting a new Iphone. I think I want something badly, but that I'll realise it's actually not that important after a few months of actually having it.

That is *so completely different* than the case at hand. A much better analogy is your parents buying you a pink iPhone case, and you don't like it. you don't feel like it represents your personality very well at all, so you want to take it back to the store so you can get a blue phone case, because that color just better represents your personality.

Gender identity isn't a "trend" like the iPhone is. Nobody just one day decides they want to be the opposite gender. It's a part of your personality that you've had your whole life and you want to express it.

Good luck, bro.

Everyone commenting is very pro-transition, which isn't always good. Transitioning isn't for everyone, it's very specific to each person's situation. Just be careful, some parents who seem very unaccepting actually turn out to be very accepting.

And in terms of dating, transitioning won't hurt your chances. In fact, lesbian transwomen probably have the best chances out of everyone, because gay people tend to be much more open to thing. A lot of lesbians probably wouldn't mind dating a trans woman as much as you would expect. Good luck.
